```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);
      transition:transform .15s,box-shadow .15s;"
      onmouseover="this.style.transform='scale(1.04)';this.style.boxShadow='0 5px 18px rgba(102,126,234,.55)'"
      onmouseout="this.style.transform='scale(1)';this.style.boxShadow='0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45)'"
    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Evidence Review: Revisiting the Performance Task

::: {.engage-box}
## 🧩 Who's at risk, and why?

At the end of each lesson, your PTO asks you to **revisit the performance task**: build a **model** with what you just figured out, then use the data to **explain how populations in the five key regions have been affected**. The three lesson evidence cards below collect what you need.

**The five regions:** Mediterranean Basin · Great Rift Valley · Japanese Archipelago · Mainland Southeast Asia · Andes Region
:::

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Earth's Interior

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🌐 Lesson 3.1: Earth's Interior

**Lesson question:** *Where did the material for new islands come from after Krakatoa erupted?*

When Krakatoa erupted in **1883**, the main island disappeared and temporary islands appeared. Since then, a new island, **Anak Krakatau** ("Child of Krakatoa"), has been growing in the same spot.

**Key evidence:**

- **Seismic waves** from earthquakes arrive at stations around the world at different times. **P waves** are slowed and bent in the middle of Earth, and **S waves** do not pass through the middle at all. S waves only travel through solids, so part of the core must be **liquid**.
- Earth is layered by **density**: a solid **inner core**, a liquid **outer core**, a semi-solid **mantle** (solid rock that flows very slowly), and a solid **crust** broken into **plates**.
- The layers are made of different rocks and minerals, with solid and liquid **iron and nickel** in the core. Earth's **magnetic field** is evidence that one layer is liquid metal.
- The **rock cycle** explains how volcanic eruptions bring material from deeper layers up to the surface, where it cools into new rock, like the new islands at Krakatoa.

📖 Review the lesson: [Earth's Interior](unit3-earth-interior.qmd)
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u3cLayers = [
  {layer: "Crust", top: 0, bottom: 35, state: "Solid", color: "#a1887f", note: "Solid rock, broken into plates. About 5–70 km thick (oceanic crust is thinner)."},
  {layer: "Mantle", top: 35, bottom: 2890, state: "Solid that flows slowly", color: "#e17055", note: "Hot rock that flows very slowly over millions of years. S waves can pass through it."},
  {layer: "Outer core", top: 2890, bottom: 5150, state: "Liquid", color: "#fdcb6e", note: "Liquid iron and nickel. S waves cannot pass through. Its motion makes Earth's magnetic field."},
  {layer: "Inner core", top: 5150, bottom: 6371, state: "Solid", color: "#f9ca24", note: "Solid iron and nickel, kept solid by enormous pressure."}
]
u3cDensity = [
  {depth: 0, rho: 2.6}, {depth: 35, rho: 2.9}, {depth: 35, rho: 3.3}, {depth: 410, rho: 3.5}, {depth: 660, rho: 4.0},
  {depth: 2890, rho: 5.6}, {depth: 2890, rho: 9.9}, {depth: 5150, rho: 12.2}, {depth: 5150, rho: 12.8}, {depth: 6371, rho: 13.1}
]
```

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Surface Features and Plate Boundaries

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🧭 Lesson 3.2: Surface Features & Plate Boundaries

**Lesson question:** *Why does seismic activity happen in some areas more than others?*

**Key evidence:**

- Earthquakes, volcanoes, and tsunamis occur in **narrow bands** around Earth. Those bands are **plate boundaries**.
- The **age of the ocean floor** is youngest at mid-ocean ridges and gets **older farther away**. New crust formed by rising magma pushes older crust away from **divergent** boundaries (plates moving apart).
- At **convergent** boundaries (plates moving toward each other), the **denser** plate sinks under the other (**subduction**). Water carried down by the sinking plate helps melt the rock above it, and that less dense magma rises to feed volcanoes. Collisions also build **mountains**.
- The **strongest earthquakes, eruptions, and tsunamis** happen at convergent boundaries, because a lot of energy builds up as plates push together.

📖 Review the lesson: [Surface Features & Plate Boundaries](unit3-plate-boundaries.qmd)
:::

Pick one of the five PTO regions to see its plate setting.

## Revisiting the Performance Task: Energy and Matter

::: {.evidence-box}
### 🔥 Lesson 3.3: Energy and Matter

**Lesson questions:** *Where is all the energy coming from to move plates apart from each other? What processes are occurring inside Earth that can cause it to reach Earth's surface? And why do people continue to live in these hazardous areas?*

The **Great Rift Valley** is the cradle of humanity: some of the oldest human fossils come from there. Yet it also has a lot of seismic activity from plates moving apart.

**Key evidence:**

- **Early Earth was extremely hot.** As it cooled, denser materials sank to the core, and less dense materials rose toward the surface. Some of those materials are **radioactive**.
- **Radioactive decay** in the mantle, plus **leftover heat from Earth's formation**, produces the heat that moves the plates.
- Heat moves out of the core by **conduction** and up through the mantle by **convection currents**. Convection and gravity move the plates, causing earthquakes and eruptions at the surface.
- Water **lowers the melting point** of rock, which helps make magma where plates subduct.
- **Tectonically active places have resources**: fertile volcanic soils, **geothermal energy**, and high concentrations of **minerals** (like copper in the Andes).

📖 Review the lesson: [Energy and Matter](unit3-energy-matter.qmd)
:::


<p style="text-align:center;font-size:.85em;"><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;background:#e17055;border-radius:2px;"></span> radioactive decay &nbsp; <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;background:#fdcb6e;border-radius:2px;"></span> leftover (primordial) heat &nbsp; <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;background:#74b9ff;border-radius:2px;"></span> all human energy use</p>

**Why do people stay?** The same processes that cause hazards also create **benefits**:

| Region | Hazard | Benefit from the same tectonic activity |
|---|---|---|
| Mediterranean Basin | Eruptions (Vesuvius), earthquakes (Turkey 2023) | Rich volcanic soils for farming (vineyards on Vesuvius and Etna), hot springs |
| Great Rift Valley | Eruptions (Nyiragongo), rift earthquakes | **Geothermal energy** (Kenya gets close to half its electricity from it), fertile lake basins |
| Japanese Archipelago | Earthquakes, tsunamis, eruptions | Geothermal power and hot springs (onsen), fertile volcanic soils |
| Mainland Southeast Asia | Collision and fault earthquakes (Myanmar 2025) | Mineral deposits like tin and gemstones, fertile river valleys fed by mountain sediment |
| Andes Region | Giant earthquakes, eruptions, tsunamis | **Copper** (Chile is the world's top producer), lithium, geothermal heat, volcanic soils |

```{ojs}
    options: ["Copper fell from space", "Magma rising at the subduction zone carries hot, mineral-rich fluids that concentrate metals in the crust", "Copper only forms in deserts", "People brought it there"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Volcanic activity moves matter from Earth's interior toward the surface. Hot fluids from magma concentrate copper and other metals in rock, which is one reason people live and work in risky areas."
  }
])
```

# Unit Closing: Earthquake Deaths Over Time

::: {.engage-box}
## 📉 Besides the hazard itself, what decides how many people die?

Return to the anchor phenomenon. Think about what, **besides** the physical risk of an earthquake, volcano, or tsunami, could affect how many people are killed: **population density**, **resources**, and the **ability to prepare** for disasters.

**Video from class:** [Stop natural hazards from becoming disasters](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6go1Gi8mP0g)

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 About these numbers

Death tolls are estimates and differ between sources, especially for older events. Haiti's toll is disputed (316,000 is NOAA's adopted figure; some sources say about 220,000). Sichuan includes people listed as missing. Magnitude is logarithmic: each whole number is about **32 times more energy**.
:::

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Volcanoes too: warnings save lives

- **Nevado del Ruiz, Colombia (1985):** scientists warned of danger, but the town of Armero was not evacuated. Mudflows killed about **23,000** people.
- **Pinatubo, Philippines (1991):** scientists monitored the volcano and tens of thousands of people were evacuated before the huge eruption. About **850** died, and thousands of lives were saved.

**Risk depends on the hazard AND on people:** how many live nearby, how buildings are built, and whether there is monitoring, warning, and a plan to act on it.
:::

## Risk Calculator

Scientists often describe risk as **Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability**:

- **Hazard:** how often and how strongly earthquakes, eruptions, and tsunamis happen (plate boundary type, seismicity, rate of plate movement, closeness to water).
- **Exposure:** how many people and how much property are in harm's way (population density).
- **Vulnerability:** how badly people are harmed when it happens (building codes, warning systems, resources). **Lower is better.**

Rate each region **1 (low) to 5 (high)** using your evidence. The calculator ranks the regions. There is no answer key: your ratings must be backed by the evidence in your PTO.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u3cRiskRegions = ["Mediterranean Basin", "Great Rift Valley", "Japanese Archipelago", "Mainland Southeast Asia", "Andes Region"]
viewof u3cRisk = {
  const factors = ["Hazard", "Exposure", "Vulnerability"];
  const value = Object.fromEntries(u3cRiskRegions.map(r => [r, {Hazard: 3, Exposure: 3, Vulnerability: 3}]));
  const form = html`<div style="display:grid;gap:10px;margin:10px 0;"></div>`;
  u3cRiskRegions.forEach(r => {
    const row = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-radius:10px;padding:10px 14px;box-shadow:0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.1);">
      <div style="font-weight:800;margin-bottom:6px;">${r}</div>
      <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;"></div></div>`;
    const box = row.querySelector("div:last-child");
    factors.forEach(f => {
      const lab = html`<label style="flex:1 1 120px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font-size:.9em;">${f}
        <select style="min-height:44px;flex:1;border-radius:8px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;padding:0 8px;background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;">${[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(n => html`<option value=${n}>${n}</option>`)}</select></label>`;
      lab.querySelector("select").value = "3";
      lab.querySelector("select").onchange = e => {
        value[r][f] = +e.target.value;
        form.value = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
        form.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
      };
      box.appendChild(lab);
    });
    form.appendChild(row);
  });
  form.value = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
  return form;
}
```

# Unit Summary

| Big idea | What the evidence shows |
|---|---|
| **Hazards cluster** | Earthquakes, eruptions, and tsunamis occur in narrow bands at plate boundaries, and people have lived in these regions for thousands of years |
| **Earth's Interior** | Seismic waves reveal layers sorted by density: solid crust, slowly flowing mantle, liquid outer core, solid inner core. Rising magma brings deep material to the surface |
| **Surface Features & Plate Boundaries** | Plates move apart (divergent) and together (convergent). Subduction zones produce the strongest earthquakes, eruptions, and tsunamis |
| **Energy and Matter** | Radioactive decay and leftover heat drive mantle convection, which moves the plates and also concentrates resources like minerals and geothermal heat |
| **Risk** | Risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability. Building codes, warning systems, monitoring, and preparedness reduce deaths from the same size hazard |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildUnit3Quiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#c0392b 0%,#e17055 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #c7d2fe;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f8f9ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
